correctness.rationale: Quantifier elimination makes the atomic equality congruence on unary terms a complete invariant. A finite quotient is isolated by its finite transition table and distinctness diagram. Conversely, any finite term diagram inside an infinite quotient can be completed to a finite unary algebra and hence embedded in an existentially closed model, so no infinite-orbit type is isolated and finite-orbit types are dense. Inside an infinite quotient, a finite represented set cannot already contain both outgoing transitions of every represented congruence class; opening such an unfixed transition to a fresh infinite ray gives two distinct infinite completions of the same cylinder. Thus the infinite locus is closed and perfect. Compact metrizability and zero-dimensionality then give Cantor space. An independent enumeration reproduced the rooted finite-orbit type counts \(1,12,216\) for orbit sizes \(1,2,3\); it is only a sanity check, not the infinite proof.

final_claim: For the complete generic theory of exactly two unary functions, a complete \(1\)-type over the empty set is isolated exactly when its generated pointed unary algebra is finite; these isolated types are countable and dense, while the first derivative is the infinite-orbit locus, is homeomorphic to Cantor space, and equals all subsequent derivatives.
